title: Cross-pair catch-up: buy the laggard after the other two pairs jump on 1h

source.title: Lead-lag relationship between Bitcoin and Ethereum: evidence from hourly and daily data

rule_summary: 1h closed candles of the three pairs; signal at bar close, order at next bar open. For pair X at bar t, let L(t) = mean of the 2-bar returns (close(t)/close(t-2) - 1) of the other two pairs, and r(t) = X's own 2-bar return. ENTRY when L(t) >= 1.5%, r(t) <= L(t) - 1.0% (X has not followed), and no position in X. EXIT at the close of the 4th bar after entry (time exit), or earlier if X closes below its entry price by 1.5% (stop checked on closed bars). Cooldown 4 bars after exit. No other filters.
mechanism: Price discovery is not instant across pairs: the source finds causality running between BTC and ETH on hourly data (mixed, and it warns that profit is hard). Smaller or less liquid pairs absorb a large move in the others with a delay because market makers and arbitrageurs re-quote them in steps, so the laggard catches up. Only large jumps (1.5% or more with a gap of 1% or more) are used, so that a catch-up of a fraction of the gap can exceed the 0.35% cost. The source gives no tradable rule; the edge is doubtful and is left for the gates to judge.
